## Purpose

Ideas takes each rough idea of the operator from capture to 1 committed, validated plan, and closes the idea when its feature is merged (G3). It decides when an idea may move to its next state, holds the operator approval gate, and answers worker questions against the approved assumptions, so that no AI plans 2 ideas at once and no task exists outside an approved plan (FR-2, FR-10, FR-12). It does not run tasks (task-execution), land branches or open the feature (integration), or start processes (worker-profiles). It owns the 1 needs-you list, where everything that waits for the operator is shown.

## Strategic classification

| Domain | Business model | Evolution |
|---|---|---|
| supporting | cost-reducer | custom |

_Strategize rationale_: supporting - G3 depends on it, and today's alternative is ideas typed into 1 orchestrator conversation; rule 3 (diff 6 with cplx 5 is below the core rule); cplx 5 because fleetd code runs 1 fixed idea state machine and the judgment work is done by the sub-orchestrator model (A1). Pattern domain-model for the plan validation module only (D1 option C, orchestrator D15): coverage, the DAG, judge pairing, the model guide and the declared gates are invariants. Intake and questions stay active-record. Medium investment: it feeds the core task-execution with committed plans. — _future_: Hidden core: the hard part (research, interview, assumptions, plan) is done by the sub-orchestrator model. Keep the dispatcher, intake and questions flat (active-record). Give plan validation an aggregate with invariant tests, and keep the approval hash under test. Review in 6 to 12 months.

## Domain roles

**specification-model**, **approver** — It builds a document, the plan, that is validated only at the hand-over event plan-committed (FR-3) and then executed by task-execution: a specification model. It holds the operator approval gate, where an idea goes on only with the operator's approved hash (FR-10, I7): an approver. Decision D2 took option A (orchestrator, D15; [define A18]).

## Ubiquitous language

| Term | Meaning in this context | Avoid |
|---|---|---|
| **Idea** | A rough request from the operator that 1 fixed state machine moves from captured to merged; only code advances it | ticket (a ticket enters as a --direct idea), request |
| **Sub-Orchestrator** | The interactive Opus 5.5 agent of 1 feature that clarifies, specifies and plans 1 idea at a time, with a fresh process per phase | orchestrator, lead |
| **Assumption** | 1 line in assumptions.md, [confirmed] or [assumed], that the operator approves or revises; also a reversible assumption that the sub-orchestrator records to answer a worker question (understand N11) | requirement |
| **Plan** | The validated plan.yaml of 1 idea: tasks, dependencies, checks, paired judges. No task exists outside a committed plan | ticket list |
| **Spec** | spec.md and requirements.yaml of 1 idea. Every requirement cites an approved assumption or an operator answer. It is written only after approval, in the phase specifying (FR-10). | — |
| **Question** | A worker question to the sub-orchestrator of its feature. It ends as an answer, an own assumption, a revise request, or an escalation to the operator | — |
| **Orchestrator** | Not a role in fleetd. The word survives only in the preserved mail contract tag [orchestrator re #<id>] (discover N3) | — |
| **Needs-you list** | The 1 place for everything that waits for the operator (design OR-3, /fleet/needs-you/): approvals, escalated worker questions and escalated tasks. ideas owns it (orchestrator, D15) | — |

## Business decisions

1. Only code advances an idea. When an idea is captured, the dispatcher starts its sub-orchestrator on the next pass and the idea goes to clarifying; a --direct idea goes to ticketing with no research and no interview (FR-1, FR-2, FR-12).
2. An idea passes awaiting_approval only when approval.json, written by fleetd, holds the sha256 of the current assumptions.md, and the approve command ran outside every fleet attempt. An approval written by any other process is ignored (FR-10, I7, C5).
3. The assumptions validator refuses assumptions.md while any item is marked [open]. When the file validates, fleetd requests the operator approval and posts a herdr notification.
4. While an idea waits on the operator, its lease is paused. After 30 min idle the sub-orchestrator process stops; after 7 days with no answer the idea goes to parked with a note in needs-you/.
5. When the assumptions are approved, or revised and approved again, the dispatcher starts a fresh sub-orchestrator process for the next phase. No phase carries a context window into the next (understand N11 keeps the decision rule of the sub-orchestrator).
6. A plan is committed all-or-nothing, and only after it passes schema, DAG, coverage, profile and citation checks; a plan for a project with no declared fast gate and full gate is refused (FR-3, FR-4). A judgment-kind task without a paired judge task in another session refuses the plan (understand N12).
7. Every requirement of an idea in in_progress or later is covered by at least 1 task that is not cancelled (I3).
8. A worker question is a ledger row with an owner, the sub-orchestrator of the feature. On each pass fleetd starts the owner if it is not running, until an answer is recorded. After 15 min with no answer from a running sub-orchestrator, the question escalates to the needs-you list, and the wait for the operator has no limit (RR-12, [define A29]).
9. The sub-orchestrator answers a question in 1 of 4 ways: cite the approved line, send a revise to the operator, replan the task, or record its own reversible assumption. Only product direction, scope or a trade-off the operator must own goes to the operator (understand N11, design decision D13). The sub-orchestrator answers through the command channel, so fleetd stays the only ledger writer.
10. When task-execution asks for a replan, the sub-orchestrator replans the task once; the replanned task goes back to task-execution as task-replanned.
11. When every task of the idea is landed on its feature branch, the idea goes to integrating. When the feature is merged and every worktree of the idea is removed, the idea goes to merged (discover N4).
12. Every feature that is not merged and not abandoned has exactly 1 live sub-orchestrator or waits on the operator (I7, I13). The dispatcher starts a missing one and stops an extra one on each pass, through worker-profiles start-agent-process (connect N3, [define A30]).
13. There is 1 needs-you list, and ideas owns it. Approvals, escalated worker questions and escalated tasks (task-escalated from task-execution) wait there for the operator; no other context shows the operator an item to decide (design OR-3, [define A25]).

## Assumptions

- [understand A3] horch earns no revenue. Its value is operator throughput: approved ideas that reach the primary branch per unit of subscription usage. (confidence medium)
- [understand A7] The alternatives are inferred from the design and the research files: today's horch with 1 orchestrator conversation, agents run by hand, and hosted merge queues (GitHub merge queue, bors, Mergify). (confidence medium)
- [understand A8] The /fleet paths in the design are a neutral layout. In horch, /fleet/ideas/<id>/ is ai_docs/plans/<run>/, /fleet/tasks/ is under the state root, and the ledger stays at ~/.horch/ledger.sqlite3. (confidence high)
- [discover A2] The idea flow has 5 phases (clarifying, planning, executing, landing, integrating) cut at 4 pivotal events (decision D1, option A, decided by the orchestrator, D15). (confidence high)
- [discover A3] Daemon supervision (stale heartbeat, restart, self-update) and adapter conformance are their own phase, operating, outside the idea flow (decision D2, option B, decided by the orchestrator, D15). The reconcile loop supervises each phase, not only executing. The operating phase has no pivotal event and no before and after on the idea timeline. (confidence high)
- [discover A4] fleetd components (idea dispatcher, verifier, landing, wrapper, reconciler) are our own system, not actors. Their commands have actor null and are issued by policies, or have the clock as actor when the reconcile pass fires them. No 'orchestrator' actor exists (understand N3). (confidence high)
- [discover A6] The event order follows understand N7 (idea states), N8 (task branch states building, verifying, ready, in_bundle, landed with side states conflicted, gate_failed, abandoned) and N9 (worktree states reserved, created, active, landing, landed, orphaned, rescued, removed). (confidence high)
- [discover A8] An idea with no --to gets its features row at capture and its feature branch at its first assumptions, so Feature Opened (the branch) happens after Assumptions Written (answer of the orchestrator, D15, to Q1 and H7). (confidence low)
- [discover A10] Event count 83 is above the standard band (25 to 60). The design has 4 state machines (idea, task, task branch, worktree) plus feature integration; merging them further hides the language conflicts H4 and H6. (confidence high)
- [decompose A2] The verifier stays a module of task-execution because it reads and writes the same task states and the reap rule (04 S7) needs 1 transaction. Decision D1, option A (orchestrator, D15). (confidence medium)
- [decompose A3] The question aggregate (worker-question-asked to question-escalated) belongs to ideas, because the sub-orchestrator answers it against the idea's assumptions. Decision D2, option A (orchestrator, D15). (confidence medium)
- [decompose A4] Worker profiles and adapters are their own context because of their rate of change and their credential rules, although the storm holds only 3 of their events (discover H14, N10). Decision D3, option A (orchestrator, D15). (confidence medium)
- [decompose A5] Worktree custody is its own context, not a part of integration, because the worktree lease and the no-loss rules differ from the branch landing rules. Decision D4, option A (orchestrator, D15). (confidence medium)
- [decompose A7] Operator attention (cap-operator-attention) maps to ideas. There is 1 needs-you list (design OR-3, /fleet/needs-you/), and ideas owns it (orchestrator, D15): approvals, interview questions, escalated worker questions and escalated tasks. task-execution emits task-escalated, and ideas puts it on the list. (confidence high)
- [decompose A11] worker-profiles owns start-agent-process and agent-process-started: it starts the fleet-run wrapper of an attempt, or the herdr pane of a sub-orchestrator, from the launch environment of the profile (discover N10). This keeps the environment scrub with 1 owner (decision D3). (confidence medium)

## Verification metrics

- Business (G3): count of tasks that exist outside a committed, validated plan, plus count of processes that planned 2 ideas at once. Target 0.
- Business (G3): count of ideas past awaiting_approval whose approved_sha256 does not match the current assumptions.md (I7). Target 0.
- Structural: count of ledger writes to ideas, plans or questions tables that come from code outside the ideas module (organise N2). Target 0.
- Structural: count of items shown to the operator for a decision from outside the needs-you list of ideas ([define A25]). Target 0.

## Open questions

- [understand Q8] This repository has no unit-only command today (research-03 F10), and plan validation refuses a project with no declared fast gate. Which command is the fast gate of this repository? Proposed answer (orchestrator, D15): the workspace tests without the crate horch-e2e. A run must confirm it.
- [discover Q3] Does an operator requeue also restore the single replan (H12)? Answered part (orchestrator, D15): an operator requeue sets the attempt count to 0, and a requeue by a review keeps its own counter.
- [discover H2 near feature-opened - conflict] 'Feature' is also a task kind (kind: feature, a code kind) and a word for any change. In fleetd a Feature is 1 sub-orchestrator, 1 feature branch and 1 pull request holding 1 main idea and its follow-on ideas. Which meaning does each document use (understand N2)?
- [discover H3 near sub-orchestrator-started - conflict] 'Orchestrator' today is 1 long-lived LLM conversation that receives ideas, creates tasks and reads mail. In fleetd it does not exist: a deterministic idea dispatcher and 1 sub-orchestrator per feature replace it. Today's mail contract still names [orchestrator re #<id>] answers (understand N3).
- [discover H7 near idea-captured - unclear] The idea row records its feature (ideas.feature_id), but the feature row and branch are written when the sub-orchestrator first writes assumptions. Which feature does an idea with no --to point at between capture and assumptions, and what does horch ideas show for it? Answered (orchestrator, D15): the idea gets its features row at capture and its feature branch at its first assumptions.
- [discover H10 near question-escalated - unclear] A worker question has 'a time limit' before it escalates, but the design gives no value for it, and it does not say if the limit pauses while the operator is outside working hours. Answered (orchestrator, D15): 15 min with no answer from a running sub-orchestrator, as a starting value. The wait for the operator has no limit.
- [connect CC2 - coupling, medium] ideas and task-execution depend on each other: plan and answer events go to task-execution, replan-requested comes back to ideas.
- [connect CC3 - coupling, medium] ideas and integration depend on each other: assumptions-written and idea-tasks-landed go to integration, feature-opened, task-branch-landed and feature-merged come back.
- [connect CC8 - coupling, medium] plan-refused is an ideas fact, but escalate-task runs in task-execution, which owns neither the plan nor the reasons.
- [connect CC9 - coupling, low] task-branch-landed has 2 consumers that need different data: worktree-custody needs the task and worktree, ideas needs the feature and idea roll-up.

## Quality attributes

| Attribute | Priority | Requirement | Scenario |
|---|---|---|---|
| integrity | high | Only the operator approves an idea's assumptions (FR-10, I7, C5). | When a sub-orchestrator writes approval.json or runs horch idea approve, then the idea stays in awaiting_approval and fleetd ignores the file. |

## Model traits and design notes

- Split by module (strategize D1 option C, [define A31]): plan validation is a domain model with the rules of coverage, the DAG, judge pairing, the model guide and the declared gates. Intake, the dispatcher and questions are active-record with invariant tests, for example the approval hash.
